title: Using Zscaler Client Connector in the Modern UI

blocks.text: Zscaler Client Connector is an application installed on your device to ensure that your internet traffic and access to your organization's internal apps are secure and in compliance with your organization’s policies, even when you're off your corporate network.

No matter where you're accessing the web, Zscaler Client Connector ensures that your traffic is forwarded to and protected by the Internet & SaaS service. You might also have the following services enabled:

blocks.item: Private Access (ZPA): Securely access your organization's internal resources from any location.

Digital Experience: Perform synthetic probing to a desired Software as a Service (SaaS) application or internet-based service (e.g., OneDrive, Gmail, etc.) to triage and pinpoint the source of performance issues.
Zscaler Endpoint Data Loss Prevention (DLP): Protect your organization from data loss on endpoints.

blocks.text: Zscaler Client Connector is designed to provide a seamless user experience. It automatically recognizes when you are connected to a trusted network (for example, your corporate office network) and depending on your organization's configuration, can disable Internet & SaaS, Private Access, Digital Experience, and Endpoint DLP services accordingly. It can also recognize when you connect to Wi-Fi hotspots (for example, at airports, hotels, and cafés) where you must pay or accept a use policy before connecting. The app disables its services for a period of time and re-enables itself after you've had a chance to complete the steps necessary to connect.

After you log in with your user ID and complete a one-step device enrollment process, you can begin safely connecting to the web and to your organization's internal applications and services with Zscaler Client Connector. To learn more, see Enrolling in the Zscaler Service on Zscaler Client Connector.

blocks.heading: Using the Zscaler Client Connector App

blocks.text: After you enroll with the Zscaler service, you can access and use the app in multiple ways, depending on your device's OS:

blocks.item: Windows
Zscaler Client Connector displays an icon in the system tray:
You can right-click the icon to access quick actions.
You can click the icon to display the home screen along with the following options:
Status Check: View the Status Orb to view the status of the security services. Possible options include:
Green: All enabled services are connected and active.
Orange: One or more of the enabled services requires user action (e.g., authentication).

Blue: One or more of the enabled services is currently unavailable. An additional message displays with more information (e.g., the internet isn't connected or a service is in the process of connecting).

Notifications: Click the Notifications icon to open the app and view the Notifications window. If you have pending notifications, a red number displays on the Notifications icon indicating the number of notifications.
Settings: Click the Settings icon to open the app and view the Troubleshooting window.
You can click anywhere in the home screen to open the app and view the Overview window:

Click the Sign Out option to sign out of Zscaler Client Connector. You might be required to enter a password your organization's admin has set for the app. If you sign out of the app, you must complete enrollment again when you log back in.
Clicking the Exit icon on the top-right corner of the app closes the app but does not sign you out, and the services continue to run.
Click Service Details to view details about the specific enabled services.
Click Notifications to view the Notifications window.
Click Settings to access the following options:
Notifications: Control how Zscaler Client Connector displays your notifications.
Troubleshooting: Perform troubleshooting actions (e.g., restarting services or reporting an issue).
Application: View information about Zscaler Client Connector.

The Overview window displays services your organization subscribes to. The following image shows that an organization has subscribed to the Internet & SaaS, Private Access, Digital Experience, and Data Protection services. If your organization is not subscribed to one of these services, you do not see that option.
The app might display in a language other than English based on your system language. To learn more, see Localization Support.
